A1.justification: Both PDFs describe D-Garment and retain the same core model and dress dataset. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original garment simulations, baseline comparisons, ablations and fitting results on captured 4DHumanOutfit sequences in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation and captured-data experiments, with additional T-shirt results and pose-history and seam-processing analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The generation backbone remains, but the fitting procedure changes substantially. v2 replaces Chamfer-plus-Laplacian fitting with robust Chamfer, an explicit collision penalty and additional normal-consistency and edge-length regularization, and introduces joint material/latent optimization (Sections 3.2 and 5.4). v1's optional temporal/collision-guided sampling branch is omitted.

E1.justification: Appendix B extends the previously dress-only simulated coverage to a separately trained T-shirt model, evaluated on an unseen sequence. This is a bounded garment-design extension within the same deformation task; the AMASS-driven dress and 4DHumanOutfit fitting tasks remain.

E2.justification: ContourCraft is added to the evaluated comparison methods in Table 2 and Figure 3. HOOD and MGDDG remain; the comparator expansion is limited to one additional method.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 expands the combined-unseen test into separate unseen-shape, motion and material tests plus an all-unseen test. Seven shape/physical metrics replace the original three, including revised surface sampling. Subdivision becomes an added evaluation variant rather than the default subdivided evaluation. Captured-data fitting changes from four sequences to two with fixed-versus-optimized material conditions.

E4.justification: v2 adds latent-noise diversity examples, fixed-versus-optimized material fitting, a five-pose extension of the existing motion-conditioning analysis, and a seam-processing ablation. It removes the guidance ablation. The mesh-resolution analysis is retained and revised in Table 3 rather than simply deleted with v1's Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, statistical confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental uncertainty estimates. v2's varying-noise examples illustrate generative diversity rather than introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The comparison and ablation results are extensively replaced and expanded. v1 Table 2 reports D-Garment CD of 2.395 cm; v2 Table 2 reports four test groups, including all-unseen ECD of 0.19 under revised conditions, so these are not direct performance gains. New T-shirt and longer-history results appear. Fitting changes from four sequence curves to material-strategy curves with 90th-percentile distances of 2.14 and 2.34 cm.

T1.justification: Localized mathematical definitions change: v1's integral curvature error is replaced by an edgewise RMS dihedral-angle error, and v2 defines additional physical metrics in Section 5.1. The fitting objective is also revised. Neither version contains a theorem/proof framework; the principal diffusion training equations remain.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the abstract's superiority claim from Chamfer distance to shape similarity and physical-validity metrics, and removes the introduction's explicit 'first approach' assertion. The model, dataset and fitting contributions remain, with template-specific training now explicitly emphasized.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses per-template retraining, capture/template mismatch and occlusions, collision-removal tradeoffs, and smoother material-optimized fittings at slightly worse target distance. It revises the subdivision interpretation toward negligible shape changes and topology-sensitive physical metrics, and explains HOOD/ContourCraft failures through their flat-rest-shape assumption.

D1.justification: v2 newly states code/data availability and supplies project and dataset access links. It adds exact corpus sizes, material initialization, fitting preprocessing and PyTorch3D implementation information. Conversely, it removes HOOD's stretching-to-Lame conversion, explicit baseline mesh sizes and the separate 50-step ablation specification. The main training recipe remains.

R1.justification: The existing positioning is extended with ContourCraft and additional simulation literature, including graph-network simulators and NeuralClothSim. New fitting/data references include Barron and GarmentCodeData, while Esser and Wallace references disappear. The central distinction between pose-dependent modeling and dynamic simulation remains.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises the abstract and portions of the introduction, related work and experimental narrative, and changes terminology to emphasize physical grounding. The main section sequence remains, with a broader-impact statement and appendices added.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. Comparison and ablation tables are substantially restructured; baseline and fitting figures are replaced or expanded. New diversity, template/capture, T-shirt and seam figures are added, while the resolution analysis is merged into the main ablation table.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for physical conditioning: separate generalization tests, broader physical measurements, ContourCraft comparisons and targeted appendix analyses address limitations of v1's combined-unseen evaluation. Explicit template restrictions and fitting tradeoffs also improve claim calibration. Although HOOD setup details disappear and captured-sequence coverage shrinks from four to two, the stronger experimental design and clearer applicability boundaries outweigh these losses.
